key_insight: Dirac-3S solves higher-order optimization natively, demonstrating an expressibility and mapping-cost advantage—not superior solution quality.
engineering_relevance: Native polynomial support can avoid the auxiliary variables, embedding overhead and two-qubit gate counts required by conventional quantum mappings.
method: Formulated four industrial use cases as six cubic and quartic optimization instances.
Ran 30 samples per instance on the hybrid photonic-electronic Dirac-3S system.
Compared results with reference objectives and estimated mapping costs for annealers and gate-based processors.
evidence_signal: All six instances yielded feasible, distinct solutions; the best portfolio result was within 0.32% of its reference, while the best budget result was 15% above its reference.
watch_item: No sample reached its reference; classical solvers reached references within minutes, and larger-scale time-to-solution advantage remains unproven.
paper_title: Native higher-order optimization with entropy quantum computing
